title: Game of Thrones
synopsis: You inherit a castle the size of a wart, on a road every army wants. Two queens want your sword, three gods want your soul, and your maester is out of wine. Welcome to the game.

nodes.text: Two ravens arrive within an hour of each other — one with a Stark direwolf seal, one with a Lannister lion. Both ask the same thing: bend the knee, or burn. Your maester pours the last of the wine and waits.

choices.text: Open the Stark raven first
choices.consequence: The North remembers — and so do its enemies. You commit to open the Stark raven first. It buys momentum toward The Direwolf's Words and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Open the Lannister raven first
choices.consequence: Gold has a longer reach than honor. You open the Lannister raven first. The route to The Lion's Coin opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: The Stark letter is short and proud — sworn swords, no gold, a place at a council table when the wars are done. Honor like a cold draft through a great hall. “Trust the cold honor of the North” draws you toward The Maester's Counsel; “Find it pretty and impractical” leaves Your Wife's Strategy waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Trust the cold honor of the North
choices.consequence: Hard ground holds up the longest. You choose to trust the cold honor of the North. By The Maester's Counsel, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Find it pretty and impractical
choices.consequence: Banners don't feed a garrison. You choose to find it pretty and impractical. By Your Wife's Strategy, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: The Lannister letter rings — a chest of dragons in advance, more after the war, a marriage with a third cousin nobody will miss. Gold has good manners. The distance between Your Wife's Strategy and The Maester's Counsel begins with the choice between “Take the coin and the comfortable side” and “Distrust gold that arrives so cheaply.”

choices.text: Take the coin and the comfortable side
choices.consequence: Survival is also a virtue, however cynical. You commit to take the coin and the comfortable side. It buys momentum toward Your Wife's Strategy and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Distrust gold that arrives so cheaply
choices.consequence: A purse this open hides a knife. You distrust gold that arrives so cheaply. The route to The Maester's Counsel opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Old Maester Edryn has served three lords and outlived two. 'There is no right answer,' he says. 'Only the answer you can live with after.' He coughs. He has, perhaps, a year. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Ask him what he would do
choices.consequence: The wise are best asked, not obeyed. You commit to ask him what he would do. It buys momentum toward The Bannermen and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Decide alone — the choice is yours
choices.consequence: A lord who borrows backbone has none. You commit to decide alone — the choice is yours. It buys momentum toward Dragon Rumors and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Lady Maren — sharper than your sword and twice as costly — lays out a map at the hearth. 'Hold the river crossing,' she says, 'and both of them will need us.' She does not smile often. She smiles now.

choices.text: Follow her plan to play both sides
choices.consequence: A bridge is the most expensive thing you own. You follow her plan to play both sides. The route to Dragon Rumors opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Refuse — call it dishonorable
choices.consequence: Honor is a kind of luxury too. You commit to refuse — call it dishonorable. It buys momentum toward The Bannermen and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Your seven small lords gather in the hall. Three are for the Starks, two for the Lannisters, one for declaring himself king of a barn, and one is asleep. Loyalty here is a candle in a draft.

choices.text: Take a vote and abide by it
choices.consequence: Democracy in Westeros is a curiosity. You take a vote and abide by it. The route to First Skirmish opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Speak first and tell them where you stand
choices.consequence: Lords lead. Bannermen follow or leave. You choose to speak first and tell them where you stand. By Wildlings at the Walls, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: A merchant claims he saw a shadow with wings the size of a longship pass over the Narrow Sea. A child claims the same. The maester scoffs and does not sleep that night. Choose “Send a man east to confirm” and First Skirmish comes into view; choose “Dismiss it as a rumor and a child” and the road bends toward Wildlings at the Walls.

choices.text: Send a man east to confirm
choices.consequence: Knowledge is the only armor that fits everyone. You choose to send a man east to confirm. By First Skirmish, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Dismiss it as a rumor and a child
choices.consequence: Dragons are stories. Until they aren't. You dismiss it as a rumor and a child. The route to Wildlings at the Walls opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: A column of mercenaries crosses your river in the night. By dawn there are dead men in the reeds — three of theirs, one of yours, a boy of fifteen who liked the cook's daughter. The war has arrived without asking.

choices.text: Hang the prisoners as a warning
choices.consequence: Cruelty travels fast and ugly. You choose to hang the prisoners as a warning. By Trial of a Traitor, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Send them home with bread and a message
choices.consequence: Mercy can be a kind of edge. You commit to send them home with bread and a message. It buys momentum toward The Spy in the Kitchen and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: A line of strangers from the North — gaunt, frostbitten, refugees from things worse than men — wait at your gates. The septon calls them savages. The cook offers them broth. “Take them in and use their strong backs” opens the route to Trial of a Traitor. “Turn them away to spare your stores” changes the terms and carries you toward The Spy in the Kitchen.

choices.text: Take them in and use their strong backs
choices.consequence: Allies arrive in odd skins. You choose to take them in and use their strong backs. By Trial of a Traitor, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Turn them away to spare your stores
choices.consequence: A castle that feeds everyone feeds no one. You commit to turn them away to spare your stores. It buys momentum toward The Spy in the Kitchen and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Your steward is caught passing word to the Lannisters. He has six children. The law is clear; the law is also a heavy weight to carry. Maren wants him beheaded by sundown. To choose “Execute him publicly to keep order” means meeting The Red Feast Invitation; “Spare him and use him as a false-message conduit” sends you toward Sermon by the River instead.

choices.text: Execute him publicly to keep order
choices.consequence: You choose to execute him publicly to keep order. By The Red Feast Invitation, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Spare him and use him as a false-message conduit
choices.consequence: A turned spy is sharper than any blade. You spare him and use him as a false-message conduit. The route to Sermon by the River opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Maren discovers a Lannister man in the scullery — leaving for two months, learning the tunnels. He kneels and begs and his accent is from a village two valleys over. “Quietly disappear the spy” opens the route to The Red Feast Invitation. “Feed him a beautiful lie and let him 'escape'” changes the terms and carries you toward Sermon by the River.

choices.text: Quietly disappear the spy
choices.consequence: Some problems vanish best at night. You quietly disappear the spy. The route to The Red Feast Invitation opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Feed him a beautiful lie and let him 'escape'
choices.consequence: Information aimed back is the cheapest weapon. You commit to feed him a beautiful lie and let him 'escape'. It buys momentum toward Sermon by the River and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: An invitation arrives, stamped with the Frey star and weighted with too much ceremony. A wedding. Both sides will be there. Maester Edryn has gone very still. You are unlikely to keep all three. Choose “Attend — refusal is its own statement” and The Wedding Hall comes into view; choose “Send your regrets and an honest gift” and the road bends toward The Marriage Pact.

choices.text: Attend — refusal is its own statement
choices.consequence: The most dangerous rooms are the most necessary. You choose to attend — refusal is its own statement. By The Wedding Hall, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Send your regrets and an honest gift
choices.consequence: Some doors are closed for the body and opened for the soul. You choose to send your regrets and an honest gift. By The Marriage Pact, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: The septon preaches that war is a punishment from the Seven for lords forgetting the small folk. Your peasants nod. So do, awkwardly, two of your bannermen. A sermon is sometimes the start of a politics. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Embrace him publicly to win the smallfolk
choices.consequence: A god on your side travels free. You choose to embrace him publicly to win the smallfolk. By The Wedding Hall, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Quietly muzzle him before he becomes a movement
choices.consequence: Sermons can outrun swords. You choose to quietly muzzle him before he becomes a movement. By The Marriage Pact, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: You ride in under your banner with a small honor guard. The hall is too full, the music is too loud, and the wine is too generous. You see Maren count exits three times. The distance between The Siege and Treaty Under Stars begins with the choice between “Leave before the toast” and “Stay and hold your position.”

choices.text: Leave before the toast
choices.consequence: You choose to leave before the toast. By The Siege, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Stay and hold your position
choices.consequence: A lord who flees a wedding becomes a story. You choose to stay and hold your position. By Treaty Under Stars, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Instead you broker a marriage of your own — your eldest to a neutral house with a tower of grain and no taste for war. Maren writes the contract; the maester signs as witness; nobody is in love. It is, by Westerosi standards, a love story.

choices.text: Make the pact public and binding
choices.consequence: Allies welded in candle-wax. You make the pact public and binding. The route to The Siege opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Keep it secret until the war declares a winner
choices.consequence: A card is sharpest when it is still face-down. You choose to keep it secret until the war declares a winner. By Treaty Under Stars, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: An army arrives — whichever army you betrayed, or didn't — and rings your walls. Inside there is food for forty days, a maester with a fever, and Maren saying, far too calmly, that she's been preparing for this her whole life.

choices.text: Hold the siege to the last grain
choices.consequence: Walls win wars patient men forget. You hold the siege to the last grain. The route to Dragon Shadow opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Negotiate from strength while you still can
choices.consequence: Speak first, before hunger does. You choose to negotiate from strength while you still can. By Northern Snows, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: On a hill between camps you meet a rival lord and a flagon of wine and a sky full of indifferent stars. Treaties under stars never quite hold to morning, but they are, sometimes, where wars actually end.

choices.text: Swear the treaty and mean it
choices.consequence: Honor offered first is harder to refuse. You choose to swear the treaty and mean it. By Dragon Shadow, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Swear it and plan to break it cleverly
choices.consequence: Cleverness comes due, eventually. You choose to swear it and plan to break it cleverly. By Northern Snows, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: A shape passes over your towers, and the temperature drops, and your archers forget what their bows are for. The dragon is real. The dragon has noticed you. The world tilts. The distance between Summons to King's Landing and Hold the Castle begins with the choice between “Kneel to whoever rides the dragon” and “Hide your house from the dragon's gaze.”

choices.text: Kneel to whoever rides the dragon
choices.consequence: Some powers you bow to without shame. You choose to kneel to whoever rides the dragon. By Summons to King's Landing, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Hide your house from the dragon's gaze
choices.consequence: Be small enough to escape notice. You choose to hide your house from the dragon's gaze. By Hold the Castle, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Word comes from the North that is worse than dragons — that the dead walk, that the Wall has fallen, that whatever color of king sits at King's Landing will not matter when winter actually arrives.

choices.text: Ride north with all your spears
choices.consequence: Some causes outrank a throne. You choose to ride north with all your spears. By Summons to King's Landing, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Fortify south and let the kingdoms cope
choices.consequence: Charity that ruins you helps no one. You commit to fortify south and let the kingdoms cope. It buys momentum toward Hold the Castle and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: A new ruler — whoever survived the wedding, the siege, and the dragon — summons you to court. The summons is silk-wrapped. You know what silk-wrapped summons mean. The paths divide here: “Attend court and play the long game” leads into The Game, Played, while “Refuse and rule your small corner well” makes A Small Lordship the next reckoning.

choices.text: Attend court and play the long game
choices.consequence: The game of thrones is for those who like rooms. You choose to attend court and play the long game. By The Game, Played, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Refuse and rule your small corner well
choices.consequence: Wisdom is also a kind of crown. You refuse and rule your small corner well. The route to A Small Lordship opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: You stand on your battlements at dawn and look out at the world you outlived. Maren joins you with two cups of cooling tea. The realm is full of corpses and kings. You and yours are still here.

choices.text: Decide to ride out and build a kingdom of your own
choices.consequence: Small lords can become large ones, given time and luck. You decide to ride out and build a kingdom of your own. The route to The Game, Played opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Decide enough is enough and live
choices.consequence: Some victories taste like an ordinary morning. You decide enough is enough and live. The route to A Small Lordship opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Burn what you cannot defend before the dragon comes
choices.consequence: There is dignity even in ash. You choose to burn what you cannot defend before the dragon comes. By Northern Snows, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Years later, in a hall hung with the banners of three dead houses, men call you Lord Paramount and bow lower than they used to. You did not start the game. You merely outlived everyone who did. Maren, beside you, hides a smile that has waited a decade.

Wars end. Kings die. Your river keeps running. You spend your old age in a hall warm with grandchildren and one fat dog, telling stories to people who don't quite believe how close you came to mattering. You laugh. They were the lucky ones.

When winter truly comes you ride north with what you have. Most of you do not return. Songs are sung about you in the long halls of houses you never knew existed. It is a small kind of immortality, but a real one.
